extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, agents, and patentees seeking or advising on extension (prolongation) of patent term and on assignments/licenses (UK context, historical Acts cited)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for applying for a prolongation or new patent term (extension of letters patent) and for registration/contents of assignments and licences under UK patent practice. Covers evidentiary, substantive and procedural criteria the Judicial Committee (Privy Council) considers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of profits from every branch of manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits from every branch of the manufacturer's operations which are fed by the patented manufacture must be brought into account when estimating the patentee's profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: assignees who manufactured dynamite and also produced nitro-glycerine and nitric acid could not exclude profits from the subsidiary manufacture. Petition dismissed where subsidiary profits were very large. (Nobel's Explosives Company example.)

rubrics_metrics.name: If patent assigned to a company, deposit company accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent has been assigned to a company, not only must the patentee's profits be shown, but the account of the company should be deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: Deacon's Patent. Practical effect: produce corporate books/accounts to evidence profits and receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show profits year-by-year including foreign receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: The profit, year by year, ought to be shown, and profits made by sales abroad must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: Perkins' Patent; Hardy's Patent. Also: profits under any foreign patents must be shown (Adair, Newton, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain absence of books of account; inability to show profits can disentitle
rubrics_metrics.description: If books of account are not forthcoming the petitioner will be required to explain their absence; if patentee has so dealt with his rights that he cannot show profits from working the patent or licences, he may be considered disentitled to an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: Markwick's Patent; Trotman's Patent; Saxby's Patent. Anti-pattern: destroying or failing to produce accounting records without adequate explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee entitled to certain personal and business expense deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking an account of profits and losses the patentee is entitled to charge for personal expenses and loss of time devoted to the patent and in endeavouring to bring the invention into use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed items include travel expenses, salaries of clerks, commissions on sales where patentee acted as salesman, and cost of making experiments. Authorities: Trotman's, Bailey's, Kay's patents, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of manufacturer's profits and allowable deduction proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits made by the patentee as manufacturer have in some cases been permitted to be deducted; in other cases they were not allowed — there is no fixed rule as to the proportion to be deducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in Hill's Patent and in certain cases two-thirds of net profits was deemed too large. Authorities show variability — courts assess on facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law expenses generally deductible except where compromise surrendered costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Law expenses incurred in maintaining patents are generally allowed in deduction of profits, but not where the patentee has compromised suits and given up costs to which he had an apparent title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: Gibbons' Patent (1 Moore). Also evidence of deductions not pleaded in petition may be inadmissible (illustration: administrator's attempt in Hallifax's Patent was disallowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new deductions not pleaded in petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Deductions from profits not mentioned in the petition or accounts cannot be allowed without admissible evidence — late claims for deductions are inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: in Hallifax's Patent, administrator's late request to deduct items not in petition was refused and evidence inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounts must distinguish expenditure on the useful part of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts should distinguish expenditure on that part of the invention which was proved useful; failure to do so may result in dismissal of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: Willcocks' Patent. Practical note: allocate costs and expenditures to the useful (patented) features specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory factors: have regard to nature and merits, profits, and all circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee must, in exercising its discretionary jurisdiction, have regard to the nature and merits of the invention in relation to the public, to the profits made by the patentee as such, and to all the circumstances of the case (s.25 Act of 1888).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central statutory rubric guiding decisions: balance public usefulness, inventor merit, and financial remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider adequacy or inadequacy of remuneration in relation to merit and circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to extend, the Committee seeks to meet the justice of the case with respect to the meritoriousness and public usefulness of the invention, and the adequacy or inadequacy of the patentee's remuneration, having regard to opportunities, adverse circumstances, and general management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patentee met with loss (and without neglect/gross mismanagement) that is prima facie ground for extension; courts will consider what the patent ought to have gained with proper management, not merely what was actually received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess inventive power and inventor's personal investment of time/trouble
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of inventive power and the time and trouble expended by the inventor in making experiments, testing, or carrying out the invention are relevant to merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small advances can be highly meritorious; however, when invention is merely a new application of a well-known simple process, smallness of step will be considered in limiting extension length (Lord Brougham's remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Smallness of step affects length of extension when invention is a simple application
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patented improvement is a small or obvious application of a well-known process, the smallness of the step will be considered in determining the length of any extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: moderate benefit to public for a simple mechanical application led to a three-year extension rather than longer term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional merit required for extensions beyond seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: To justify an extension for a longer time than seven years, the invention must be clearly shown to possess a very-exceptional degree of merit and public usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical practice: some cases recommended ten years where exceptional; full 14-year extensions are very seldom granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior foreign patent or importation may bar extension (historical rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent was obtained for an invention imported from abroad and previously patented in a foreign country, earlier decisions held that the British patent became void at the expiration of the foreign patent and extension applications were refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: Aubé's, Poolers, Adair, Hills'. Note: the text states the Act having been repealed alters applicability to newer patents, but earlier voiding may still affect pre-Act patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to grant a new patent with conditions instead of simple prolongation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Committee reports favourably, the patent may be extended for seven (or exceptionally fourteen) years, or a new patent may be granted for time specified with any restrictions, conditions and provisions thought fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new patent is usually dated the day after expiration of the original term and is subject to the Act; persons using the invention in the interval are not liable for infringement; investors who worked the invention in the interval may attend to oppose or seek protection for their expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend only specific heads of invention when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent comprises several heads of invention and only one head seems deserving of prolongation, the prolongation will be granted solely with reference to that head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: Leaver's Patent, Lee's Patent, Napier etc. Practical implication: tailor any extension/new patent to the particular claims/parts meriting protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert protective conditions in new patent where assignment was for inadequate consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patentee has assigned his interest for an inadequate sum relative to likely future profits, the Privy Council may insert a condition in the new patent making it void if a fixed annual sum or a certain share of profits is not paid to the patentee by the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: Whitehouse's, Hardy's, Morton's Patents. This is a tool to protect inventors who may have been undervalued at assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant prolongation to patentee alone when mortgaged
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patentee had mortgaged his patent and both patentee and mortgagees asked for prolongation, it was granted to the patentee alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: Bovill's Patents. Alternatively, special arrangements (e.g., trust for personal representatives) may be required in particular circumstances (Herbert's Patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee may impose other special conditions (price, licence terms, Admiralty use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions sometimes introduced into a new patent include obliging the patented article to be sold at a certain price, that licences be granted on certain terms, or that the Admiralty may use the invention without licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and authorities provided; Committee may refuse to insert some conditions (Lancaster's, Carpenter's cases). Use conditions to protect public or specific interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Once prolongation granted, no further extension by the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prolongation of a patent term has once been granted, the jurisdiction of the Judicial Committee is exhausted and they have no power to entertain an application for a further extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority: Goucher's Patent. Practical consequence: apply for the full appropriate extension at once; further relief unlikely from same forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit office copy at Patent Office to enter in register
rubrics_metrics.description: When an order has been made for extension or grant of a new patent, an office copy of such order must be forthwith left at the Patent Office so it may be entered in the register (see Rule 74 of the Patents Rules 1890).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to complete the administrative effect of the extension/new patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs are in Committee's discretion; allocation depends on conduct and merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of all parties incident to proceedings for extension are in the discretion of the Judicial Committee; orders respecting costs are enforceable as court orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles: frivolous opposition may lead to costs awarded to patentee; difficult/doubtful cases generally do not produce costs to successful petitioner; a properly conducted successful opposer may receive costs; petitioners who abandon applications may be ordered to pay costs; lump sums sometimes awarded to opposers; taxing officer may allow or disallow payments to scientific witnesses at discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit, profits, losses and equitable considerations illustrated by cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers balance degree of utility/merit, amounts already realised by patentee/assignees, losses suffered (e.g., by fire, piracy, litigation), prior discovery/novelty issues, capital invested, and practical ability to work the invention when determining extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected cases illustrate application: Kay (three years granted despite profits), Roberts (seven years after extraordinary losses), Morgan (refused where assignees profited), Muntz (profits from manufacture count toward patentee's reward), Jones (lack of novelty leads to refusal and costs), Derosne (six years for great public benefit), Stoney (ten years for exceptional circumstances). Use these cases as templates for evidentiary presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register assignments and licences promptly; registration formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable to register both assignments and licences as soon as may be after execution; rules 67–72 prescribe procedure: written request to Comptroller and original instrument plus attested copy to be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assignment is not registered an assignee cannot maintain an action for infringement against third parties except licensees from the assignor subsequent to and with notice of the assignment. The Act of 1852 practice was simpler; abide by Patents Rules 1890 (Rules 67–77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment instrument formalities (deed; covenants)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a valid instrument an assignment ought to be a deed under hand and seal. It is usual to include covenants that the patentee is the true and first inventor and that the patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where assignor does not part with entire interest, include covenant binding him not to seek leave to amend the specification or drawings without written consent of assignee. Practical drafting guidance for assignments.
